## What the examiners keep saying.

**The nine recurring messages (M23–M26 general and chief examiner's comments):**

| # | Message | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Answer the requirement asked; excluded or unrelated topics earn nothing | M26 Q5 (TP excluded; residence/migration), M23 Q3 (DPT for loans), N24 Q5 (hybrids with no trigger), M26 Q3 (holdover), M24 Q3 (pre-sale loss relief) |
| 2 | Do not restate the question or pad | M26 Q1 (CIR admin, PIE) |
| 3 | Bank the easy marks on each question | General comments |
| 4 | Show workings: marks are available even when the figure is wrong | N23 Q5, M25 Q4 |
| 5 | Use a conventional CA layout | M24 Q2, N23 Q3 |
| 6 | Give a recommendation when asked | M23 Q2 |
| 7 | Use the supplied treaty extract, not the OECD Model | N23 Q1 |
| 8 | "Tax consequences" means all syllabus taxes; a named tax means only that tax | N25 and M26 chief examiner |
| 9 | Keep £ and £000 consistent | M26 Q4 |

**The trap atlas** (gathered from this book's Exam lens boxes; evidence from the examiners' reports):

| Topic | Trap | Sitting | Chapter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Roll-over | Chargeable on **proceeds not reinvested**, not the gain | N24 Q1, M26 Q3 | 16, 17 |
| Leases | Short-lease status at the **transaction date**; an **assignment is not a grant**; use the lease table | N24 Q1, N25 Q5, M26 Q3 | 16 |
| Indexation | Cannot create or increase a loss; capital losses never against income | M25 Q5, N25 Q5, M26 Q4 | 16, 18 |
| Group transfers | NGNL = transferor's cost, not market value; but appropriation from stock is at market value | M23 Q4, N25 Q5 | 17 |
| Fixtures | s 198 values go into the CA pool; adjust gains only for a loss | M23 Q4, N25 Q5 | 9 |
| Full expensing | Disposals give a balancing charge (or a split) | M23 Q1, N24 Q4, M26 Q2 | 8 |
| FYAs | The balance after a 40% or 50% FYA joins the pool **after** that period's WDA, so it gets no WDA until the next period (CAA 2001 s 58(5)) | book (marking-guide logic) | 8 |
| HP | Whole capital element in the pool when brought into use | M26 Q2 | 8 |
| SBA | Price paid excluding land and integral features; pre-29 October 2018 buildings: alterations only; 1/12th not 1/9th | M25 Q4, N25 Q4, M26 Q2 | 9 |
| CFC | 25% test ≠ control; stop at the first exemption; low profit margin; apportion creditable tax; say how the charge works | M24 Q5, M25 Q1, M26 Q5 | 26 |
| Consortium | Limit by the member's share of the **consortium company's** profit; link company; DRIC; liquidation | N24 Q2 | 15 |
| Depreciatory transactions v value shifting | The former "do not consider motive and only apply to losses"; the latter is "motive based"; exempt distributions excluded | N24 Q3 | 17 |
| R&D | Linked enterprises; RDEC steps in order (step 1 v step 2) | M24 Q4 | 10 |
| QIPs | Very large rules; true up when forecasts change; count associates on the day before the AP | M25 Q2 | 3 |
| Enquiries | Large-group windows; a long period of account shifts dates | M25 Q6, N25 Q4 | 3 |
| Tax strategy, SAO | Use the accounts for the year ending in the parent's FY; SAO counts **UK-incorporated** companies only | M25 Q3, N23 Q5 | 4 |
| CIR | Interest TP adjustments reduce ANTIE, not tax-EBITDA; adjust both for a QIC; no group ratio when told not to | M26 Q1 | 28 |
| DTR | Royalties for one asset paid from several jurisdictions are one source, credits aggregated (TIOPA 2010 s 47) | N25 Q1 | 24 |
| Migration | Land acquired after 5 April 2019 automatically postponed; payment plans | N25 Q3 | 22 |
| Branches | Incorporation gain postponement; election irrevocable, covers all PEs, timing for losses; anti-fragmentation | M23 Q2, N25 Q2, M26 Q5 | 23, 25 |
| DPT | Do not raise it for loans; now repealed (UTPP, awareness) | M23 Q3, N23 Q1, N24 Q5 | 30 |
| Deferred tax | Liabilities always provided; loss asset can offset; no b/f balances for a new company; short-term differences; compute the charge | M24 Q2, M25 Q2, N25 Q1, M26 Q6 | 6 |
| Entertaining and gifts | Employee limits irrelevant to the CT deduction; branded drink disallowed, pens allowed | M26 Q4, N24 Q4, N25 Q1 | 7 |
| Pensions | Spread only when the rules are triggered | N25 Q1 | 7 |
| Marginal relief | Deal with straddles; "whilst the marginal rate of tax between the thresholds is 26.5%, this is not the rate that should be applied in full" | M24 Q6, M26 Q4 | 7 |
| Stamp taxes | Add-on marks routinely missed; stamp duty ≠ SDLT | N25 Q5, N23 Q2 | 21 |
| Stamp duty on earn-outs | A capped contingent consideration is charged on its **stated maximum** (contingency principle) | book | 21 |
| Earn-out receipts after an SSE sale | Later receipts are disposals of the earn-out right (*Marren v Ingles*): chargeable on the generally accepted view, not settled law | book | 18, 20 |
| Blocked foreign trade receipts | A trading receipt that cannot be remitted is relieved under CTA 2009 ss 173–175, not Part 18 (which is for other foreign income) | book | 25 |

On DTR the N25 examiners put it starkly: "Nearly all candidates failed to realise that the royalties can be treated as one source and the foreign tax credits aggregated." The statutory basis is **TIOPA 2010 s 47**: where double taxation arrangements apply, royalties for one asset paid from more than one foreign jurisdiction are treated as income from a single asset (chapter 24; N25 Q1 itself involved no treaty, and the examiners took the same approach under unilateral relief). On CFCs, after M26 Q5 they criticised "not mentioning obvious points (e.g. how CFC legislation works)": two lines on how the charge works and who pays it are almost free marks.

> **Exam lens: compliance questions**
> - **Frequency:** compliance and governance appeared eight times M23–M26 (N23 Q5, M25 Q3, M25 Q6, M24 Q3(c), N24 Q5, N25 Q4(a), M26 Q1(a), N23 Q1(b)): a 10–15 mark "admin" question is very common.
> - **The traps are counting:** QIP associates on the day before the AP (marginal relief: any time in the AP) (chapters 1 and 3); large-group enquiry windows; tax strategy on the accounts for the year ending in the parent's FY; SAO on UK-incorporated companies whatever their residence (chapter 4).
> - **Note:** a summary of the N24 Q5 marking guide describes QIP thresholds as divided by "51% group companies". The law since 1 April 2023 divides by **associated companies** (control test); answer on that basis (chapters 1 and 3).

## Learning from the papers.

For each sitting the CIOT publishes the question paper, suggested answers with a marking guide, and the examiners' report. **M24 to M26 also publish example candidate scripts banded by mark (40–50, 50–60, 60–70, 70+).** Read a script that scraped a pass next to one over 70 on the same question: the difference is rarely knowledge, usually coverage, precision and layout. (Note: the M26 examiners' report PDF is headed "November 2025" on page 1, a CIOT typo; its content is May 2026.)

**Topic frequency, M23–M26 (42 questions; derived from the papers):**

| Topic | Main focus or major part | Chapters |
|---|---|---|
| Full CT computation | Every sitting (M23 Q1, N23 Q4, M24 Q6, N24 Q4, M25 Q2, M25 Q4, N25 Q1, M26 Q4), often with a QIP and tax-charge tail | 3, 5–7 |
| Capital allowances and SBA | Standalone M24 Q2, M26 Q2, N23 Q3(b); embedded in nearly every computation | 8, 9 |
| Property gains, leases, group roll-over | 5 (M23 Q4, N24 Q1, N25 Q5, M26 Q3, M26 Q4) | 16, 17 |
| Shares: SSE, pooling, reorganisations, earn-outs | 5 (N23 Q2, M25 Q5, M24 Q3, N24 Q3, N23 Q4) | 18 |
| Groups and consortia | 6 (N24 Q2, N24 Q3, M23 Q5, M24 Q3, M26 Q4, M24 Q6) | 15, 17 |
| International (residence, PE, branch exemption, migration) | Every sitting since N24 (M23 Q2, N23 Q1, N24 Q6, N25 Q2, N25 Q3, M26 Q5) | 22–25 |
| CFC | 4, including two full 20-mark questions (N23 Q1(c), M24 Q5, M25 Q1, M26 Q5) | 26 |
| Transfer pricing | 5 (M23 Q3, N23 Q6, M25 Q4, N24 Q5, M26 Q1) | 27 |
| CIR | 4 (M23 Q3, M24 Q1, M26 Q1, M24 Q6) | 28 |
| Compliance and governance | 8 | 3, 4 |
| R&D | 3 (M24 Q4, M25 Q2, N25 Q1) | 10 |
| Tax accounting | 4 (M24 Q2(b), M25 Q2(b), N25 Q1(b), M26 Q6) | 6 |
| Loan relationships and derivatives | 4 (M23 Q6, M24 Q6, N23 Q3, N25 Q4) | 12 |
| Investment companies | 4 (M23 Q6, M24 Q1, M25 Q5, M26 Q4) | 13 |
| Hybrids | 1 (N25 Q6, 10 marks) | 29 |
| Not seen M23–M26 | Patent Box, DPT, Pillar Two, demergers, transactions in securities, liquidations, CCO, DOTAS/GAAR, standalone IFAs | 4, 11, 19, 30 |

**Favourite combinations** (this book's cross-references mirror them): CT computation + CAs + losses + QIPs + deferred tax; TP + CIR (M23 Q3, M26 Q1, N24 Q5), where a TP settlement years later can require a revised interest restriction return whose extra relief may be stranded by group relief time limits (Tarnmoor's GY6, chapters 27 and 28); PE + branch exemption + incorporation + CFC (M23 Q2, N25 Q2, M26 Q5); residence + CFC (N23 Q1); property gains + roll-over + fixtures election + CAs + SDLT (M23 Q4, N25 Q5); sale of a subsidiary + degrouping + SSE + change of ownership + enquiries (M24 Q3); investment company + group relief + lease premiums (M26 Q4). Chapter 31, on the Ridgeway deal, showed the method for a question that touches many regimes at once.

**Silence is not safety.** Demergers, transactions in securities, liquidations, the CCO and the GAAR are core or non-core and could appear at any sitting.

**The programme around the paper (ACA CTA Joint Programme, for ACA registrations from 1 July 2025):**

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Order | **PR&E must be passed before** the AT or APS paper; TKS before or at the same sitting as the specialist paper; the CIOT strongly recommends TKS first, then the specialist paper at a later sitting |
| Validity | AT/APS pass valid **7 sessions** (TKS 7; PR&E 9); JP registration lasts 4 years |
| Failing | You may switch to another specialist paper in the same route instead of resitting, subject to your employer |

**Pass rates (LCG AT):**

| Sitting | Passed / sat | Pass rate |
|---|---|---|
| M23 | 202 / 288 | 70% |
| N23 | 133 / 219 | 61% |
| M24 | 191 / 309 | 62% |
| N24 | 150 / 255 | 59% |
| M25 | 212 / 328 | 65% |
| N25 | 181 / 269 | 67% |
| M26 | 274 / 371 | **74%** |

(Derived: 1,343 of 2,039 over the seven sittings, about 66%.) The M24 chief examiner reported that Joint Programme candidates had the highest pass rates. Reassurance, not a promise: CFC apportionment (M25 Q1) and group relief over two years (N24 Q2) were answered poorly.

**Before your sitting, check:** (1) the **2027 grid** and **2027 prospectus** (none published as at October 2026); (2) the **2027 tax tables** (expected to show FA 2026: 14%, 40% FYA); (3) your date and slot on your entry confirmation.

**After your sitting (context only).** From **May 2028** the CTA changes. LCG AT continues (3.5 hours; four to six questions of 10, 15 or 20 marks). CIR, hybrids and IFAs fall to **2**; gains on leases, derivatives beyond basics, EOTs/EBTs and R&D-intensive SMEs leave the syllabus; close companies arrive at 2. A new learning outcome: "Critically evaluate and communicate the output of information generated by other parties or by Artificial Intelligence". None of this applies to a 2027 sitting, which stays under the current grid; the JP-specific form of the paper from 2028 is not yet published.

---

## What to take away.

- **The paper:** 3 hours 30 minutes; normally six questions of 10, 15 or 20 marks (usually three 20s, two 15s, one 10); 100 marks; pass mark 50%; at least 70% of the CT element from core. Listed groups with no controlling individual. Technical prose and computations, never a letter.
- **The day:** 4 May 2027, 2.30pm (fallback 26 October 2027; check your confirmation). Arrive early; no entry after 30 minutes late; no leaving in the first 45 or last 10 minutes. No watches. Physical calculator. Note paper is not marked.
- **RM Assessment Master:** "Calculations left in the spreadsheet and not copied to the answer box will not be marked"; formulae are invisible. Copy every working across, labelled. The timer flashes 10 minutes before the end: the only warning.
- **Resources:** tax tables (paper and PDF), the OECD Model (2017 articles, PDF only), Croner-i or Tolley legislation (tags, no notes, no pro formas). A supplied extract beats the Model. The 2026 tables show 18%; FA 2026 law is 14%.
- **Time:** 2.1 minutes a mark (derived): 42 / 31½ / 21 minutes. Half time at 4.15pm. Bank the easy marks; move on.
- **Requirements:** calculate, explain, discuss, recommend. "Tax consequences" = every syllabus tax; a named tax = that tax alone. Excluded means excluded.
- **Marks:** 0.5–1 per point; many short precise points, each with its authority; show workings; state any assumption and carry on.
- **Layouts:** conventional, one unit per table.

**So what does this paper reward?** Not what you know, but what you show: the right rule, applied to these facts, laid out where the marker can see it, inside the time.

Next, the conclusion steps back from the exam and from Tarnmoor, and asks what the whole of the larger company's tax system adds up to.

---

# Conclusion.

The book began with one loan and two answers. A company called LLC5 borrowed about $4bn from its own group. Transfer pricing asked whether strangers would have lent on those terms, and said yes. The unallowable purpose rule asked why the company borrowed, and took every pound of the deductions away (*BlackRock HoldCo 5, LLC v HMRC* [2024] EWCA Civ 330). The Supreme Court refused permission to go further.

Thirty-two chapters later, that case looks less like a puzzle and more like a summary. A larger company lives under several rules at once, each asking its own question. The adviser's job is to know which questions are being asked, and to ask them all.

This conclusion does four things. It answers the four questions the book set out with. It revisits the debates the book has carried. It looks at what is coming, separating what is law from what is only proposed. And it asks what a large group's tax function will look like in the years after your exam. The law it describes is the law for **FY2026**, and the facts about what is coming are as they stood on **9 October 2026**, when this book was finished.

## One taxpayer or many.

The law's answer has not moved since *Salomon v A Salomon and Co Ltd* [1897] AC 22 (HL). A company is a person distinct from its members. Each company in a group computes its own profits, files its own return and pays its own tax, on its own timetable. There is no group return.

What the law does is build bridges, each with its own guest list; and it refuses to build others. The refusals are where the marks are.

| Bridge | Group test | Refusal or limit (the exam point) | Tarnmoor (invented) | Chapter |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Group relief (CTA 2010 Part 5) | 75% + economic ownership | Overlapping period; lower of surrenderable and available; s 105(3A) threshold (gross profits + apportioned CFC profits) for ME, property losses, QCDs, NTIFA losses | TEL GY2 group and consortium relief £17,095,000; TPLC's £825,000 a year of ME stranded | 13, 15 |
| Carried-forward losses (Part 5A; Part 7ZA) | 75% | Own use first; £5m group allowance; 50% restriction; no Part 5A surrender of a joiner's pre-acquisition losses for 5 years | — | 14, 15 |
| Change of ownership (Part 14) | >50% | Major change in nature or conduct of trade (Ch 2) | Brackenwell's £8.6m lost | 14 |
| No gain/no loss (TCGA s 171) | Gains group (75% / effective 51%) | Degrouping charge (s 179) within 6 years; pre-entry losses (Sch 7A) | Calder's works to TES; water-systems factory to TWS | 17 |
| Group roll-over (s 175) | Gains group | Proceeds not reinvested chargeable | Depot: £800,000 chargeable | 16, 17 |
| SSE (Sch 7AC) | 51% group holding | Trading conditions; para 15A hive-down only inside a group (*M Group*) | Coldwater; TAL | 18, 20 |
| Shared allowances | AIA (parent undertaking); deductions allowance (nomination) | One allowance to share; nil without a nomination | £1m AIA; £5m to TEL | 8, 14 |

Yet the newest rules lean the other way:

- the **CIR** takes the **worldwide group** as its unit and asks how much interest the whole group may deduct in the UK (TIOPA 2010 Part 10);
- **Pillar Two** measures the group's effective rate **territory by territory**, across all its entities there (F(No.2)A 2023 Parts 3–4);
- for chargeable periods beginning on or after **1 January 2026**, most UK-to-UK dealings are taken out of transfer pricing altogether (TIOPA 2010 s 164A), because inside one country the price between relatives usually changes nothing.

**Answer:** many taxpayers for computing and paying; one business for an increasing number of the limits.

## Where profits are made.

| Layer | Rule | Tarnmoor (invented) | Chapter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Presence: residence | Incorporation (CTA 2009 s 14) or central management and control; treaty tie-breaker (s 18); exit charge (TCGA s 185) | TIL migrates 30 June GY4: CT £850,000, plan £525,000 in 6 × £87,500 | 22 |
| Presence: PE | Fixed place or dependent agent; for chargeable periods beginning on or after 1 January 2026, "principal role" in concluding contracts (CTA 2010 s 1141, FA 2026 Sch 7) | TVS: domestic PE in GY4, no treaty PE | 23 |
| Sharing | Treaties allocate and limit; DTR credit capped at UK tax on the income | Calder's Vallarian project: £180,000 credited; top-up £45,000 | 24 |
| Exemption | Branch exemption by election (CTA 2009 s 18A) | Calder did not elect; Ridgeway Cycles elects for its Dublin branch | 25, 31 |
| Drift: TP | Arm's length (TIOPA 2010 Part 4) | Know-how re-priced £6.0m → £8.0m; MAP relief in Vallaria | 27 |
| Drift: CFC | Only profits diverted from the UK (Part 9A) | TPLC's charge on TCM: £204,000 (GY5) | 26 |
| Drift: interest | Net interest capped at 30% of tax-EBITDA, subject to the debt cap (Part 10) | Disallowed £2.21m (GY1), £2.30m (GY2) | 28 |
| Drift: hybrids | Mismatch outcomes neutralised (Part 6A) | Project Undertow rejected | 29 |
| Drift: pricing backstop | UTPP charge at 31% (main rate + 6%) for APs beginning on or after 1 January 2026; DPT repealed | — | 30 |
| Floor | 15% per territory: IIR (MTT), DTT, UTPR | TPLC's top-up on Marrovia: £102,000 (GY5) | 30 |

**Answer:** profits are taxed where the activity and the decision-makers are, and the law has built a series of fences against their drifting elsewhere. The latest fence is not a wall at the border. It is a minimum, set by agreement among many countries.

## What the law follows.

All three, in layers:

1. **The accounts first.** CTA 2009 s 46 starts trading profits from GAAP; loan relationships, derivatives and intangibles follow profit or loss. *HMRC v NCL Investments Ltd* [2022] UKSC 9: a properly computed accounting debit counts unless a statute removes it. A change of accounting standard can change taxable profit without a Finance Act (chapter 5).
2. **The deal second.** A share exchange is not a disposal (TCGA s 135); a scheme of reconstruction passes assets across without a charge (s 139); an exempt demerger is not a distribution (CTA 2010 s 1075 onwards). The law respects the form of a commercial transaction if its conditions are met (chapters 18–19).
3. **Purpose last, overriding both.** s 441 CTA 2009 (*BlackRock*, *Kwik-Fit*, *JTI*); the rewritten share exchange test in TCGA s 137 for issues from 26 November 2025, after *Delinian* (formerly Euromoney) won in the Court of Appeal in November 2023; s 139's purpose test reaching income tax; s 31 value shifting; ss 184A–184I; CTA 2010 Part 14B; the treaty principal purpose test; UTPP's tax design condition.

**The trend:** mechanical rules are steadily acquiring purpose tests.

## Governing the tax, and spotting the issue.

The law gives everyone a part:

| Who | Duty | Source | Chapter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Senior accounting officer | Appropriate tax accounting arrangements; annual certificate | FA 2009 Sch 46 | 4 |
| Board / head of group | Publish the tax strategy | FA 2016 Sch 19 | 4 |
| Company | Notify uncertain tax treatments (two triggers; >£5m) | FA 2022 Sch 17 | 4 |
| Company (criminal) | Failure to prevent facilitation of tax evasion; defence of reasonable prevention procedures | Criminal Finances Act 2017 ss 45–46 | 4 |
| Tax function | The calendar: QIPs, returns, CIR returns, TP files, CbC, Pillar Two registration and returns | Various | 3, 27, 28, 30 |

The adviser's part is the one the CIOT names: identify the issues, explain them precisely, coordinate the specialists. Chapter 31 showed what that means. One modest acquisition, of Ridgeway from Jess Hartley, touched stamp duty, instalments, transfer pricing, the SAO, the CIR, Pillar Two, R&D, deferred tax, a retention bonus and a foreign branch. None of those points was hard alone. The skill was to find them all, and then to answer the one question Jess had left open: Ridgeway Cycles elects for the branch exemption.

## The debates, revisited.

The book has tried to give each side at its strongest, and to say where the law or the evidence stands, without offering a verdict on live politics.

| # | Debate | One side | The other side | Where the law stands (FY2026) | Chapters |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Separate entity or single economic unit? | Certainty; respect for legal form | Matches how groups work | Separate entity start; CIR and Pillar Two adopt unit measures | 1, 15, 28, 30 |
| L2 | Reach of unallowable purpose | Ordinary acquisition finance with a tax benefit should be safe | A factual question about each company's purpose | HMRC won *BlackRock*, *Kwik-Fit*, *JTI* (2024); *Syngenta* pending before the UT | P, 12, 28 |
| L3 | Is arm's length the right test? | The only test countries share | Treats integrated groups as strangers | Arm's length across borders; s 164A exemption at home | 27, 26, 30 |
| L4 | Anti-diversion taxes outside CT? | Pay first, outside treaties (DPT; *Glencore*) | Treaty-compatible CT | DPT repealed; UTPP keeps pay-first inside CT | 30, 23 |
| L5 | A global minimum tax | Ends the race to the bottom | Complexity; sovereignty; incentives | Enacted (MTT, DTT, UTPR); side-by-side package **proposed, not law** | 30, 26 |
| L6 | Interest restriction design | Simple, internationally shared ratio | Debt–equity bias; administrative burden | 30% fixed ratio; FA 2026 simplified reporting company appointment | 28, 12 |
| L7 | R&D relief | Incentive value | Fraud and error | Merged scheme; claim notification; additional information form | 10 |
| L8 | CFCs and EU law | Protect the UK base | Freedom of establishment; State aid | 2012 regime built partly in answer to *Cadbury Schweppes*; Commission's State aid decision annulled by the CJEU (2024, as reported) | 26, 2 |
| L9 | Should tax follow the accounts? | Audited, consistent, cheap | Accounting choices move tax | It does, subject to statute (*NCL*, *GDF Suez*) | 5, 6, 12 |
| L10 | Does transparency change behaviour? | Disclosure deters | Evidence still thin; burden | SAO, strategy, UTT in force; UTT widening **proposed, not law** (consultation 12 March–4 June 2026) | 4, 27 |
| L11 | Territoriality | Exemption matches where value is created | Credit protects the base | Dividend exemption (2009); elective branch exemption (2011); compulsory exemption **proposed, not law** | 25, 24, 26 |
| L12 | Certainty or fairness? | Purpose tests catch what mechanics miss | Answers depend on evidence of motive | Purpose tests spreading; clearances the partial answer | 18, 19, 4 |

None of that applies to a 2027 sitting. It shows where the profession thinks the work is going.

## The tax function to come.

The rules already enacted give a fair picture of a group like Tarnmoor over the next few years.

- **A data function.** Pillar Two returns need figures from every entity in every territory, 15 months after the year end (18 for the first). CbC reports, Master Files and Local Files need the same discipline. If the ICTS regulations are made, transaction data will travel with the return; if HMRC's tagged computations arrive, the computation itself becomes data HMRC's systems read before any person does.
- **A governance function.** The SAO certificate, the published strategy and UTT put the tax function's controls before the board and before HMRC's customer compliance manager (TCRM1000: risk ratings shared with the group). The corporate criminal offence puts its procedures before the courts.
- **A function of specialists, coordinated.** No single person knows every regime in this book at depth. The group head of tax, like our invented Tom Hesketh, knows enough of each to see the issue, ask the right specialist and put the answers into one recommendation for the board.
- **A function that checks.** Much of the first draft of tax work (the research memo, the summary of a new rule, the first pass at a computation) will increasingly come from software, including AI. The CIOT's 2028 learning outcome describes the job that remains: evaluate that output critically; go back to the statute; check the date the law applies from; say whether a point is law, HMRC's view, disputed or proposed.

## The living law.

The book's title is a claim. Corporate tax law is not a finished code. It is a set of answers to questions that keep changing, as groups grow, borders matter in new ways, accounts are rewritten and governments agree new floors. The four questions will still be asked after the rules that answer them today have changed.

So for the exam, keep the law for FY2026, and use it precisely. After the exam, keep the questions. Is this one taxpayer or many? Where was this profit made? What is the law following here? And what must this group do, by when, and what would a good adviser flag?

The last piece of this book is a note on sources: where the law in these chapters lives, what this book could not open, and how to keep up once the exam is behind you.

# A note on sources.

Every rule in this book came from somewhere. This note says where. It describes the places corporate tax law lives and how to read them, it says plainly what this book could not open while it was being written, and it suggests how to keep up once the exam is behind you. The law described throughout is the law for **FY2026**, and the facts in this note are as they stood in **October 2026**.

## The statute book.

The law itself lives on **legislation.gov.uk**, the free official site run by The National Archives. Every Act this book relies on is there:

| Act | Citation | URL pattern (section) | Short name in the audio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Corporation Tax Act 2009 | 2009 c. 4 | legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2009/4/section/441 | the two thousand and nine Act |
| Corporation Tax Act 2010 | 2010 c. 4 | legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2010/4/section/1141 | the twenty ten Act |
| Taxation (International and Other Provisions) Act 2010 | 2010 c. 8 | legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2010/8/section/371BC | the International Act |
| Taxation of Chargeable Gains Act 1992 | 1992 c. 12 | legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1992/12/section/171 | the Gains Act |
| Capital Allowances Act 2001 | 2001 c. 2 | legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2001/2/section/51C | the Capital Allowances Act |
| Taxes Management Act 1970 | 1970 c. 9 | legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1970/9 | the Management Act |
| Finance Act 1998 Sch 18 (company returns) | 1998 c. 36 | legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1998/36/schedule/18 | the company return rules |
| Finance (No. 2) Act 2023 Parts 3–4 (Pillar Two) | 2023 c. 30 | legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/30 | the Pillar Two legislation |
| Finance Act 2026 (Royal Assent 18 March 2026) | 2026 c. 11 | legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2026/11 (add /enacted for the text as passed) | the Finance Act twenty twenty six |

**Revised and enacted.** The **revised** text shows the law as later Acts have amended it; the **enacted** text shows exactly what Parliament passed. You need both: the revised text tells you what a section says now; the enacted text tells you what an amending Act did and, through its commencement provisions, from when. Those provisions often sit at the end of a Schedule, far from the section they govern (for example, the UK-to-UK TP exemption's start date is in FA 2026 Sch 6 para 32: chapter 2).

**The "Changes to legislation" box.** Read it before you rely on any revised page. It gives the date up to which the text is "up to date with all changes known to be in force", and lists effects the editors have not yet applied. The site itself warns that revised legislation "may not be fully up to date". When the box lists outstanding changes, the words on your screen may not be the law.

**Point-in-time versions.** You can read a section as it stood on a chosen date; for most legislation the record starts on **1 February 1991**. Tax law applies by period, so a 31 March company and a 31 December company can be under different versions of the same section on the same day (chapter 2's three-company example on CTA 2010 s 1141).

**Statutory instruments and treaties** live on the same site: SI 1998/3175 (instalment payments), SI 2004/3256 (Disregard Regulations), SI 2004/3271 (change of accounting practice), SI 2016/237 (CbC), SI 2023/818 (TP records). Treaties reach a company's return through Orders in Council under TIOPA 2010 s 2.

## Judgments.

Court and tribunal judgments are published free by The National Archives through **Find Case Law** (caselaw.nationalarchives.gov.uk), launched in **April 2022**. Search by case name, neutral citation, judge, court or date. The neutral citation is the quickest key: *BlackRock HoldCo 5, LLC v HMRC* [2024] EWCA Civ 330 is at caselaw.nationalarchives.gov.uk/ewca/civ/2024/330.

Coverage of older decisions is uneven, so for an older case you may need the court's or tribunal's own pages, or the older free archive, BAILII. Two habits matter more than the source:

1. **Read the judgment, not a summary.** The paragraph that decides your point is rarely the one a newsletter quotes.
2. **Check what happened next.** A tribunal decision can be reversed, and an appeal may still be pending (*Syngenta Holdings Ltd v HMRC* [2024] UKFTT 998 (TC), Upper Tribunal appeal pending when this book was finished).

## HMRC's manuals and guidance.

HMRC publishes its internal manuals on GOV.UK (gov.uk/hmrc-internal-manuals). The ones this book drew on most:

| Manual | Code | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| International Manual | INTM | Treaties, DTR, PEs, branch exemption, CFCs, transfer pricing |
| Corporate Finance Manual | CFM | Loan relationships, derivatives, the CIR |
| Company Taxation Manual | CTM | Groups, losses, instalments, distributions, demergers |
| Corporate Intangibles Research and Development Manual | CIRD | Intangibles, R&D, Patent Box |
| Capital Gains Manual | CG | Company gains, groups, SSE, reorganisations |
| Capital Allowances Manual | CA | Plant, SBA, fixtures |
| Senior Accounting Officers Guidance | SAOG | SAO |
| Tax Compliance Risk Management | TCRM | HMRC's large business risk ratings |
| Stamp Taxes on Shares Manual / SDLT Manual | STSM / SDLTM | Stamp duty, SDLT |

Each manual has an **updates** page, and many pages carry banners where the law has moved faster than the guidance (for example the INTM transfer pricing pages after FA 2026). Around the manuals sit **policy papers**, **consultation documents and outcomes**, and **tax information and impact notes (TIINs)**, which say what a measure is for and whom it affects.

**Status.** A manual is **HMRC's view, not law**. A tribunal is not bound by it, and where it conflicts with the statute, the statute wins. Where this book relied on a manual it says "HMRC's view is" or "HMRC's guidance says". But departing from HMRC's known position can, for a large business, create a duty to notify under the UTT rules (FA 2022 Sch 17; chapter 4). So the manuals are not law, and they still matter.

## The OECD's texts.

The OECD publishes the **Model Tax Convention and Commentary**, the **Transfer Pricing Guidelines** (2022 edition, published 20 January 2022), the **2010 Report on the Attribution of Profits to Permanent Establishments**, the BEPS reports of 2015 (including Action 2 on hybrids and Action 4 on interest), and the model rules and guidance behind **Pillar Two**.

For most of the code these texts are **persuasive**: in *Fowler v HMRC* [2020] UKSC 22 the Supreme Court said the Commentaries carry persuasive force "as the cogency of their reasoning deserves" (chapter 2). But for chargeable periods beginning on or after **1 January 2026**, FA 2026 writes them into UK law in three places:

| Rule | Statute | OECD text referred to | Later versions? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Transfer pricing | TIOPA 2010 s 164 | Model Art 9 (approved 18 November 2025); TP Guidelines 2022 | Yes, "as amended or replaced from time to time", subject to Treasury opt-out |
| Attribution to a PE | CTA 2009 s 20 | Model Art 7 and Commentary; 2010 Attribution Report; TPG 2022; March 2018 guidance | Yes, as above |
| Definition of a PE | CTA 2010 s 1140A | Model Art 5 and Commentary (approved 18 November 2025) | Not confirmed whether later versions are followed (chapters 2, 23) |

The 2025 update to the Model was approved by the OECD Council on **18 November 2025** and published the next day; revised full editions were expected in 2026.

**In the exam** the position is simpler: you are given the **2017 articles** of the Model as an on-screen PDF, and a **supplied treaty extract beats it**.

## What this book could not open.

A source note should be honest about its gaps.

**1. The OECD's own texts.** The OECD's website could not be opened while the book was written. The book has not read the TP Guidelines, the 2025 Model and Commentary, or the 2010 Attribution Report in their full original form. Where it describes them, it relies on the statute that refers to them, HMRC's descriptions (chiefly INTM), and published summaries, and says so where the point matters. The Commentary changes approved in November 2025 (for example, new paragraphs 44.1–44.21 on Article 5 on when a home office can be a PE) are known here only from professional summaries. A reader who needs the exact words of a Guideline or Commentary paragraph should go to the OECD's own publication.

**2. Examination documents not yet published.** As this book was finished, the CIOT had published no **2027 syllabus grid**, no **2027 prospectus** and no **2027 tax tables**. Every grade in the Exam lens boxes comes from the **2026 grid**. The 2025-to-2026 grid comparison was made against the **draft** 2025 grid (January 2024), because the final 2025 grid could not be found. The **transitional rules** for the 2028 CTA changes were also unpublished.

**3. The method of checking.** For this edition, much of the verification relied on **search results that quote primary sources** (legislation.gov.uk, GOV.UK manuals, Find Case Law, CIOT pages), rather than on reading the full text of each source. A search result shows an extract, sometimes truncated. The labels follow from that:

| What was seen | How the book states it |
|---|---|
| Clear extract of statute or judgment | "The law says" / "the courts have held" |
| HMRC manual text only (statute not seen) | "HMRC's view is" / "HMRC's guidance says" |
| Secondary reports only (commentators, press) | Attributed ("commentators put the deductions at about £654m"; "as reported") |
| The book's reasoning from the sources | "On this book's reading" |

Examples to calibrate by (check each against the full text in your own legislation product before relying on it for a client):

- **Associated companies for QIPs counted on the day before the AP begins** rests on HMRC's manuals (CTM92530, COM95001); the amended text of SI 1998/3175 reg 3 was not found (chapters 1, 3).
- **Payments for a surrendered RDEC ignored for tax** rests on HMRC's description of the new rule; the full text of FA 2026 s 31 was not seen (chapter 10).
- **The 3-month window for a required revised CIR return** (TIOPA 2010 Sch 7A para 8(4)) was seen in HMRC's guidance (CFM98645), not in the statutory text itself (chapter 28).

**4. The invented case.** Everything about Tarnmoor, its people, numbers and countries (Vallaria, Marrovia) is invented. Real cases, statutes and dates are real. The invented case never stands in for a real one.

## Keeping up after the exam.

Tax law moves on an annual cycle.

| Stage | When | What to read | 2026 example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Budget | Autumn | Budget documents, policy papers, TIINs | **28 October 2026** (not yet happened as at 9 October 2026) |
| Legislation Day | Usually July | Draft clauses and technical consultation (GOV.UK collection) | **13 July 2026**: "Finance Bill 2026-27 draft legislation and technical tax documents"; consultation closed 7 September 2026 |
| Finance Bill | After the Budget | The Bill, explanatory notes | Finance Bill 2026-27 (the Budget will confirm its final contents) |
| Finance Act | Often spring | Enacted text and commencement provisions | FA 2026: Royal Assent 18 March 2026 |

Watch each measure's commencement words: "periods beginning on or after" a date is not the same as "payments made on or after" it.

**Where to look:**

- **Law:** legislation.gov.uk; the GOV.UK collection for each Finance Bill.
- **Judgments:** Find Case Law.
- **HMRC's thinking:** manual update pages; GOV.UK consultations; HMRC's Large Business pages ("HM Revenue and Customs: Large Business") and the TCRM manual on risk reviews.
- **Professional bodies:** the CIOT's *Tax Adviser* magazine (monthly, with a Technical Newsdesk section) and its weekly technical email to members; CIOT submissions and Finance Bill briefings; the ICAEW Tax Faculty's weekly newsletter **TAXwire** and monthly **TAXline**.
- **Firms:** Budget-day and Legislation-Day briefings. Use them as maps, then go back to the text.
- **International:** the OECD's announcements on Pillar Two and on the Model and Guidelines (FA 2026 now imports later versions of the TP Guidelines automatically, subject to the Treasury opt-out).
- **The exam:** the CIOT's tax tables page, syllabus and prospectus pages (2027 grid and tables), and key dates page.

And whatever the source, keep the habits this book has tried to teach: find the primary text; check the date it applies from; say whether a point is law, HMRC's view, disputed or only proposed; and when a summary arrives from someone else, or from software, read it as the 2028 learning outcome will ask, critically, against the source.

That is the end of the book. The law will keep living. You now know where to find it.
